In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the temporal resolution available with X-ray scattering techniques at third generation light sources can be improved by a factor of at least 10.
the temporal resolution of the experiment is not limited by the duration or the intensity of the X-ray pulse but is determined by the time scale of the dynamics under study.
the temporal resolution of synchrotrons is limited by the pulse duration and not by the bunch length.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have demonstrated the possibility of obtaining ultrafast structural dynamics from a set of synchroton X-ray diffraction images by deconvoluting the X-ray pulse.
we have demonstrated that the timing protocol can be used to extract structural dynamics from the scattering signal with a time resolution of 20 ps.
we have demonstrated the feasibility of the technique, and that it can be applied to study ultrafast structural dynamics.
The main takeaway from our work is that
it is not only the duration of the X-ray pulse but also its temporal shape which determines the temporal resolution of an experiment.

it is possible to retrieve structural information with temporal resolution that is faster than the duration of the X-ray pulse, by walking the timing of the femtosecond pump pulse through the X-ray pulse.
it is possible to obtain structural information from ultrafast processes using synchrotron light, which are not limited by the duration (or the timing precision) of the X-ray pulse.
